correctness.rationale: The face geometry is reconstructed directly from equality in Hölder’s L1–L∞ inequality. Its distance formula is proved by aligned/unaligned mass splitting with an attaining face vector. The gap constant is established by the exact defect decomposition and sharp densities on complementary near-maximizer sets; its divergent case uses an essential supremum, not finite attainment. The strong orthogonality criterion is proved in both directions with small-parameter norm bounds; the gapless counterdirection uses an explicit bounded sign function. Boundary regimes B null, r=0, r=1 and A null are distinguished. Rational checker replay agrees in 14,772 finite mass tests; no infinite conclusion relies on enumeration.

originality.rationale: Full text of Choi–Jung–Kim (arXiv:2208.11987v1, Definition 1.2 and Theorems 2.13/2.15) establishes a sufficient isolated-level construction and dense counterexamples but not a necessary and sufficient classification for every probability L1 nor the sharp global face-error constant. The present conclusions are not implied by the classical Bhatia–Šemrl results for scalar L1, which involve a stronger and different antecedent. The later general numerical-range work does not furnish the same measure-level classification or coefficient. Published-record searches returned related nonidentical norm-attainment and face formulas; residual unindexed-equivalence and inaccessible-full-text risks remain.
residual_risks: The full 2019 Kim–Lee article was not accessible despite lawful routes; an uninspected equivalent metric statement cannot be ruled out.
Norming-face metric regularity may be described by generic convex weak-sharp-minimum terminology outside orthogonality indexing.
Published-search and metadata comparison cannot establish global uniqueness or access unpublished work.

value.rationale: Adjusted Bhatia–Šemrl membership is a natural geometric property introduced in 2022, and the complete necessary/sufficient criterion was not among the inspected source conclusions. Its equivalence to finite norming-face metric regularity is quantitative, with exact optimal coefficient, a discontinuous all-plateau value and blow-up as the complement approaches norm one. This gives a usable classification for mixed atomic/nonatomic L1 spaces and pinpoints how near-maximizing but nonattaining values destroy stability, beyond the source’s density constructions.
